title: Build live dashboards and animate explainers with Claude
summary: Anthropic announced Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion. Dashboards generate live, plain-language reports from BigQuery, Snowflake, Databricks, and Salesforce that refresh with the data and link numbers to their queries (beta on paid plans), while Motion creates editable animations from a prompt that can be exported as MP4 (beta on Team and Enterprise). Docs, Slides, and Design have left beta and are available on all plans including Free, Claude Design has moved into conversations, and claude.ai/design closes December 14.

title: Claude Code in the cloud: a field guide to cloud sessions
summary: Cloud sessions run Claude Code on an isolated VM with the repo cloned to a new branch, and the output is a branch or pull request. They can be started from claude.ai/code, mobile, Desktop, the terminal (`claude --cloud`), or Slack, and they run without your laptop so parallel tasks do not collide. The GitHub token stays outside the VM, `~/.claude` config does not carry over (so repo CLAUDE.md should hold shared settings), and sessions are included in Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise while sharing usage limits.

title: How Comcast and Booz Allen use Claude Mythos to find exploit chains and secure their codebases
summary: Security teams used Mythos-class models through Project Glasswing to find, validate, and fix vulnerabilities that scanners missed, reasoning across code, configuration, identity, and live behavior to surface exploit chains. Comcast found a critical authentication flaw across 258 systems and about 170M lines of code and fixed it before exploitation, with validation now the bottleneck, while Booz Allen traced a pre-boot flaw and had one analyst cover 8 systems and 138 repos in 12 days. Both accounts stress that human validation and remediation ownership remain essential.

title: We're expanding the Claude Startups program to help founders build
summary: The Claude Startups program is opening to more founders building on Claude. Perks include a free year of Claude Team (up to 5 Premium seats), $1,000 in API credit, and Applied AI office hours, plus a new Claude Startup Stack with partner tool discounts and credits worth up to $45,000. Startups founded within the last 5 years or funded within the last 2 years are eligible, and the program includes help listing products on the Claude Marketplace.

title: Claude Haiku 5.5
summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 (`claude-haiku-5-5`), its cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model, priced at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens for prompts up to 100k. It is about 75% cheaper than Haiku 4.5 on average and is the first Haiku-class model with an adjustable effort setting. The release also halves the Sonnet 5.5 cache-read price and adds monthly API credits for Max and Team subscribers, and it suits support, browser use, and subagents, while Sonnet and Opus 5.5 remain better for complex agentic coding.

title: Building effective agent automations
summary: A guide and reference implementation shows how to build scheduled agents on Claude Managed Agents (beta), using a daily Slack and GitHub brief example that is deployed with `ant apply`. It covers six parts (sources, destination, agent config, schedule, memory stores, and guardrails) and reliability patterns such as per-source bookmarks, re-checking live status, and recording a send only after Slack confirms it, along with credential vaults and a per-run budget cap of 3-5x normal cost. These patterns matter because scheduled agents tend to fail quietly, and they target those silent failure modes.
